text: In a circle, the angle in a semi-circle is a right-angle, and that in a greater segment (is) less than a right-angle, and that in a lesser segment (is) greater than a right-angle. And, further, the angle of a segment greater (than a semi-circle) is greater than a right-angle, and the angle of a segment less (than a semi-circle) is less than a right-angle. Let $ABCD$ be a circle, and let $BC$ be its diameter, and $E$ its center. And let $BA$, $AC$, $AD$, and $DC$ be joined. I say that the angle $BAC$ in the semi-circle $BAC$ is a right-angle, and the angle $ABC$ in the segment $ABC$, (which is) greater than a semi-circle, is less than a right-angle, and the angle $ADC$ in the segment $ADC$, (which is) less than a semi-circle, is greater than a right-angle.
Let $AE$ be joined, and let $BA$ be drawn through to $F$.
And since $BE$ is equal to $EA$, angle $ABE$ is also equal to $BAE$ [Prop.~1.5].
Again, since $CE$ is equal to $EA$, $ACE$ is also equal to $CAE$ [Prop.~1.5].
Thus, the whole (angle) $BAC$ is equal to the two (angles) $ABC$ and $ACB$.
assertion: angle BAC equals sum of angles ABC and ACB

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the whole (angle) $BAC$ is equal to the two (angles) $ABC$ and $ACB$

text: And $FAC$, (which is) external to triangle $ABC$, is also equal to the two angles $ABC$ and $ACB$ [Prop.~1.32].
assertion: angle FAC (external angle of triangle ABC) equals sum of angles ABC and ACB

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $FAC$, (which is) external to triangle $ABC$, is also equal to the two angles $ABC$ and $ACB$

assertion: angles BAC and FAC are each right-angles

text: Thus, the angle $BAC$ in the semi-circle $BAC$ is a right-angle.
assertion: angle BAC in the semi-circle BAC is a right-angle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the angle $BAC$ in the semi-circle $BAC$ is a right-angle

text: And since the two angles $ABC$ and $BAC$ of triangle $ABC$ are less than two right-angles [Prop.~1.17], and $BAC$ is a right-angle, angle $ABC$ is thus less than a right-angle.
assertion: angle ABC is less than a right-angle

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the two angles $ABC$ and $BAC$ of triangle $ABC$ are less than two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: angle $ABC$ is thus less than a right-angle

text: And it is in segment $ABC$, (which is) greater than a semi-circle.
assertion: angle ABC is in segment ABC, which is greater than a semi-circle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: it is in segment $ABC$, (which is) greater than a semi-circle

text: And since $ABCD$ is a quadrilateral within a circle, and for quadrilaterals within circles the (sum of the) opposite angles is equal to two right-angles [Prop.~3.22] [angles $ABC$ and $ADC$ are thus equal to two right-angles], and (angle) $ABC$ is less than a right-angle. The remaining angle $ADC$ is thus greater than a right-angle.
assertion: angle ADC is greater than a right-angle

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: $ABCD$ is a quadrilateral within a circle

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the (sum of the) opposite angles is equal to two right-angles

spans.label: glue
spans.text: [Prop.~3.22] [angles $ABC$ and $ADC$ are thus equal to two right-angles], and

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: The remaining angle $ADC$ is thus greater than a right-angle

text: And it is in segment $ADC$, (which is) less than a semi-circle.
assertion: angle ADC is in segment ADC, which is less than a semi-circle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: it is in segment $ADC$, (which is) less than a semi-circle

text: I also say that the angle of the greater segment, (namely) that contained by the circumference $ABC$ and the straight-line $AC$, is greater than a right-angle. And the angle of the lesser segment, (namely) that contained by the circumference $AD[C]$ and the straight-line $AC$, is less than a right-angle.

assertion: the horn angle claims are immediately apparent

text: For since the (angle contained by) the two straight-lines $BA$ and $AC$ is a right-angle, the (angle) contained by the circumference $ABC$ and the straight-line $AC$ is thus greater than a right-angle.
assertion: the angle contained by circumference ABC and line AC is greater than a right-angle

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the (angle contained by) the two straight-lines $BA$ and $AC$ is a right-angle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the (angle) contained by the circumference $ABC$ and the straight-line $AC$ is thus greater than a right-angle

text: Again, since the (angle contained by) the straight-lines $AC$ and $AF$ is a right-angle, the (angle) contained by the circumference $AD[C]$ and the straight-line $CA$ is thus less than a right-angle.
assertion: the angle contained by circumference AD[C] and line CA is less than a right-angle

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the (angle contained by) the straight-lines $AC$ and $AF$ is a right-angle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the (angle) contained by the circumference $AD[C]$ and the straight-line $CA$ is thus less than a right-angle

text: Thus, in a circle, the angle in a semi-circle is a right-angle, and that in a greater segment (is) less than a right-angle, and that in a lesser [segment] (is) greater than a right-angle. And, further, the [angle] of a segment greater (than a semi-circle) [is] greater than a right-angle, and the [angle] of a segment less (than a semi-circle) is less than a right-angle. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
